run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/fraud-detection since 2026-11-18T02:01:13Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The alert on otel-demo/fraud-detection is explained by error spans that are all client calls from fraud-detection to the flagd feature-flag service: operation flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream, error=true, otel.status_code=ERROR, rpc.grpc.status_code=4 (DEADLINE_EXCEEDED), each lasting ~594-602 s and starting 01:09:50-01:14:47. In the same traces flagd (v0.12.8) server spans carry otel.status_description 'stream closed due to server-side timeout' on 2 of 9 streams, while 7 ended with rpc.grpc.status_code 0. The same EventStream pattern appears in ad (10 grpc-4 error spans, 3 flagd server spans with server-side-timeout text) and recommendation (3 spans with explicit StatusCode.DEADLINE_EXCEEDED text, flagd server spans code 0 at 599.999 s), so the failing element is shared flagd streaming, not fraud-detection's own message handling: its 'orders receive'/'orders process' consumer spans in the trace sample have no error status. fraud-detection is otherwise up (10/10 pods Running, restartCount 0) and flagd is Running/ready with 0 restarts; flagd was re-rolled at 01:07:07 via kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt with an unchanged pod template and the same image digest label, and all fault flags in ConfigMap flagd-config read defaultVariant 'off'. Conclusion is partial: the object where the failures are produced is flagd, but no setting or change record explains why flagd ends EventStreams after ~9-10 minutes, metrics stop at 01:29-01:31 so the alerting instant 02:01:13 is unobserved, and application logs for both fraud-detection and flagd returned no lines.

claims.text: Prometheus holds only two metric names for label service_name="fraud-detection" in 01:00-02:14: traces_span_metrics_calls_total and traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket; no rpc_/http_/kube_ series are present, so the error-rate signal is span-derived.

The summed ERROR counter for service_name="fraud-detection" rose only on flagd operations: span_name=flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream status_code=STATUS_CODE_ERROR went 1 (01:21) -> 6 (01:22) -> 10 (01:24) and stayed 10 through 01:30, and flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveInt error went 1 -> 2; the non-error consumer counters orders receive/orders process rose from 10/12 to 221/230 in the same samples (sample times 01:18-01:31, then the series reset).

All 10 error=true traces returned for fraud-detection in 01:00-02:14 have a fraud-detection span of operation flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream with status tags error=true, otel.status_code="ERROR", rpc.grpc.status_code="4" and durations 594,101,234-601,796,702 us; the spans start 01:09:50.6Z to 01:14:47.5Z (source range of the query: 01:09:50-01:21:36).

In the same traces the server side is service="flagd" version v0.12.8: 9 flagd spans of operation flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream (durations 549,003,096-556,200,065 us), of which 2 are error=true with rpc.grpc.status_code="4" and otel.status_description="stream closed due to server-side timeout" (span ids 7a4ab60e782bfb14 and ea20c7808d335aa4), while 7 recorded rpc.grpc.status_code="0".

The identical EventStream failure appears in other flagd clients: ad has 10 client spans of flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream with rpc.grpc.status_code="4" (durations 596.9-604.2 s) and 3 flagd server spans with "stream closed due to server-side timeout"; recommendation has 3 spans of /flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream with status_description/exception message 'StatusCode.DEADLINE_EXCEEDED' and grpc_status:4, whose flagd server spans ended with rpc.grpc.status_code="0" after 599.999 s. The 01:30 ERROR counters show ad/flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream=10 and recommendation//flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream=7.

Kubernetes state at query time: the fraud-detection Deployment has replicas=10 and its 10 pods (fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-*) are all phase Running, ready, restartCount 0; flagd-58db7486bd-2plsx is phase Running, ready, restartCount 0, created/started 2026-11-18T01:07:07Z/01:07:09Z.

flagd has two ReplicaSets: flagd-c47676d99 (created 01:05:14, replicas 0) and flagd-58db7486bd (created 01:07:07, 1 ready replica); their pod templates are identical (same image ghcr.io/open-feature/flagd:v0.12.8, same command and env) except the annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-18T01:07:07Z on the newer one, while every other otel-demo ReplicaSet was created 01:05:13-01:05:15.

ConfigMap flagd-config key demo.flagd.json declares 12 flags, all state ENABLED with defaultVariant "off" (adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak 0, imageSlowLoad 0, kafkaQueueProblems 0, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage 0, paymentFailure 0, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure); none references fraud-detection. flagd runs /flagd-build start --port 8013 --ofrep-port 8016 --uri file:./etc/flagd/demo.flagd.json with GOMEMLIMIT 60MiB and limits cpu 250m/memory 512Mi, and fraud-detection uses FLAGD_HOST=flagd, FLAGD_PORT=8013.

Cluster events inside the authorized window mention no flagd or fraud-detection object: the otel-demo events are Deployment recommendation ScalingReplicaSet (10->8 at 01:21:07, 8->7 at 01:22:07), ReplicaSet recommendation-5f45f75855 SuccessfulDelete x3 and Pod Killing x2 for recommendation pods; other events are HorizontalPodAutoscaler failures and data-recorders PVC/job events.

Primary explanation: fraud-detection's RequestErrorRate is driven by its flagd EventStream client calls that end as DEADLINE_EXCEEDED (rpc.grpc.status_code 4) after ~600 s; the server-side spans of flagd in those traces show the stream was closed on the flagd side ('stream closed due to server-side timeout'), so the error originates in the flagd streaming dependency and surfaces as errors attributed to service fraud-detection.

Alternative, not excluded: a ~600 s client-side deadline on a long-lived server-streaming call converts normal long stream lifetimes into ERROR spans - recommendation's flagd server spans ended with rpc.grpc.status_code="0" at 599.999 s while the client span recorded DEADLINE_EXCEEDED at 600.006 s - so part of the error rate may come from client-side stream-deadline configuration rather than from flagd failing.

Secondary candidate: the flagd rollout at 01:07:07 (kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt, unchanged pod template, same flagd image, new ReplicaSet flagd-58db7486bd) could have changed how EventStreams behave, since the first failing fraud-detection stream starts 01:09:50, ~2.7 min after the new flagd pod started; however no failing stream exists before the restart in the retained data, so a causal link is unproven and the trigger of the restart is not visible.

fraud-detection's ordinary message handling shows no errors in the sampled traces: 20 'orders receive' and 20 'orders process' spans from 01:21:18-01:22:26 have status_state not_recorded and durations 427-98,812 us, so the error rate is not coming from the order-consumption path in that sample.

flagd itself was up and serving: its pod is Running and ready with restartCount 0, its Deployment has 1 ready replica, and 7 of the 9 flagd EventStream server spans recorded rpc.grpc.status_code="0" - the observed failure is a stream-duration/timeout pattern, not flagd being down or unreachable.

Rejected: fraud-detection pods crashing, restarting or being evicted/OOMKilled. All 10 fraud-detection pods are Running, ready, restartCount 0, events contain no Unhealthy/Evicted/OOMKilled/Failed for them, and the error spans are client calls to flagd rather than the service's own consumer operations.

Rejected as far as the declared configuration shows: a switched-on fault-injection flag aimed at fraud-detection. Every flag in ConfigMap flagd-config (demo.flagd.json) has defaultVariant "off" and none names fraud-detection or its flagd path; only runtime values changed through flagd-ui would be invisible.

Rejected: Kafka pod restarts and the recommendation scale-down explain the fraud-detection error rate. kafka-ff7884766-lbw2w (3 restarts, last container exit code 1 at 01:16:36) and kafka-ff7884766-vg9vr (1 restart, exit code 1 at 01:11:39) changed in the window and recommendation was scaled 10->7, but fraud-detection's observed error spans are exclusively flagd client calls and no error status was observed on its Kafka consumer spans.

gaps: The alerting instant is unobserved: an instant query of sum by (service_name,span_name,status_code)(rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="fraud-detection"}[5m])) at 2026-11-18T02:01:13Z returned no series (status no_data), and all trace-metric samples end at 01:29:22-01:31:00, so the alert's current value 0.02222 cannot be reproduced from data at 02:01.

No Prometheus alerting rule named RequestErrorRate exists in the target (list_prometheus_rules rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned nothing), so the alert expression, ratio denominator and threshold are unknown.

Application logs are unavailable: fetch_pod_logs on flagd-58db7486bd-2plsx and fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-2m24l for 01:00-02:10Z returned 0 lines (no previous container instances exist), so no log evidence from either side.

flagd emits no traces_span_metrics series of its own (query {service_name="flagd"} in 01:00-01:35 returned nothing), so flagd's own error/latency metrics and its request denominators are unknown; only sampled Jaeger spans describe flagd.

kube-state-metrics series are absent from this Prometheus ({__name__=~"kube_.*"} and kube_deployment_status_replicas_available/ready for flagd and fraud-detection returned nothing), so no historical replica/readiness timeline exists; Kubernetes findings rest on object state at query time (~02:15), not at incident time.

The change_history integration is not available, so who or what applied kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-18T01:07:07Z to flagd and when ConfigMap flagd-config last changed cannot be determined.
flagd's effective runtime flag values (which flagd-ui can change) could not be read; only the ConfigMap defaults (all 'off') are visible.

The trigger of flagd's ~9-10 minute EventStream termination, and whether it is a flagd server setting, a resource constraint (GOMEMLIMIT 60MiB, cpu limit 250m) or client deadline, is not established; flagd logs and flagd metrics were not obtainable.

Unattributed changes inside the window: kafka-ff7884766-lbw2w (3 restarts, last exit code 1 at 01:16:36), kafka-ff7884766-vg9vr (1 restart, exit code 1 at 01:11:39), recommendation HPA scale-down 10->7 (01:21-01:22) and HorizontalPodAutoscaler FailedGetResourceMetric/FailedComputeMetricsReplicas events; none could be tied to fraud-detection's error evidence.

Other services in the same span metrics also carry ERROR counters (e.g. frontend GET 327-349, frontend-proxy ingress 432-433, checkout oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 13-14, payment GET 20, shipping 12, accounting orders receive 5); these were not investigated and are not attributed to this alert.

Jaeger data is a sampled view (error search returned 10 traces, non-error search 20 traces; Jaeger keeps the newest 5000 traces) and events cover only 01:20:32-01:24:45, so completeness of the error population and of the pre-01:09 period is unknown.
next_steps: Inspect flagd's configuration and version defaults for a server-side EventStream/keepalive deadline in flagd v0.12.8, and check whether the length of the deadline matches the observed ~9-10 minute stream ends.
Audit flagd-ui actions/audit trail and the runtime flag values in flagd, since ConfigMap defaults show all flags off and the runtime state could differ.
Compare the EventStream gRPC deadline configured in the fraud-detection (Go), ad and recommendation (Python) clients to confirm whether ~600 s is a client deadline on a long-lived stream.
Retrieve Prometheus samples after 01:31 (up to the 02:14 window end, ideally at 02:01:13) to confirm the error rate behind the alert and whether the flagd EventStream errors continued.
Evaluate flagd resource pressure during 01:00-02:00 (GOMEMLIMIT 60MiB with 250m CPU / 512Mi limits) and check for CPU throttling or GC stalls on flagd-58db7486bd-2plsx.
Check with the change owner who issued the flagd rollout restart at 2026-11-18T01:07:07Z and whether the flagd-config ConfigMap was edited at the same time.

As advisory noise reduction, consider excluding long-lived server-streaming spans such as flagd EventStream from the RequestErrorRate ratio, or fixing the stream deadline, if the timeout is confirmed to be a deadline artifact rather than a flagd fault.
